sources.title: Introducing Structured Outputs in the API
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026, including Under the hood and Availability. The exact August 6 snapshot was trained for schema adherence; constrained decoding and lower API prices are described, without a nominal total or active parameter count. Dated August 6, 2024 and explicitly states gpt-4o-2024-08-06 was released that day. Describes the new snapshot training for schema adherence, function tools and JSON-schema response formatting. This is the exact August snapshot, not the May GPT-4o launch.

sources.title: GPT-4o model documentation
sources.evidence: Rechecked October 27, 2026 using the freshly fetched complete Markdown and official documentation retrieval. The gpt-4o alias explicitly defaults to gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and specifies 128,000 context, 16,384 maximum output, text/image inputs, text output, function calling and file uploads. Neither total nor active parameters are specified. August snapshot is Deprecated; May snapshot is separately Shut down. The explicit alias mapping binds these specifications to the August snapshot.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: February 18, 2026 guide by an OpenAI author, read in HTML and full Markdown. Section 2.1 explains OpenAI caching through Transformer attention stacks; section 2.2 explicitly includes gpt-4o. Applied to the documented default August snapshot, this supports broad Transformer structure, not complete block inventory, routing or counts. Archived applicability is pre-GPT-5.6.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Prompting Guide
sources.evidence: Complete Markdown fetched. The none-reasoning-mode section explicitly identifies GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 as prior non-reasoning models. It distinguishes absence of dedicated reasoning tokens from visible prompted reasoning.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Complete Markdown explicitly names gpt-4o as a vision-capable model for PDF ingestion, where extracted text and page images are sent to the model. Combined with the current alias binding and file-upload support, this verifies PDF as API document input rather than a separate native modality.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: October 14, 2026 notice explicitly lists gpt-4o-2024-08-06 for API shutdown January 14, 2027. Scheduled retirement is distinct from completed shutdown and from the separate May snapshot retirement.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: Indexed first-party article read after direct page retrieval timed out. August 5, 2025 release identifies gpt-oss as the first open-weight language models since GPT-2 and calls GPT-4o proprietary. Its parameter and architecture table describes gpt-oss only.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current agreement grants limited service access and reserves service intellectual property in sections 2.2 and 9.1. Supports the descriptive Proprietary classification for the hosted API model; not a checkpoint license or a claim these precise January 2026 terms applied at the 2024 launch.

sources.title: Toward understanding and preventing misalignment generalization
sources.evidence: Reopened the original PDF from the October 27, 2026 fresh cache and searched its complete extracted text. Appendix G.3 explicitly identifies full fine-tuning of gpt-4o-2024-08-06. Appendix D.1 and Table 3 describe an auxiliary sparse autoencoder: 2.1 million latents and 64 non-zero latents per token. Those are SAE hyperparameters, not GPT-4o total or active production parameters. No nominal production count or dense/MoE routing disclosure was found.

sources.title: GPT-4o System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened the full official system card on October 27, 2026, inspected Introduction and Model data & training, and searched parameter terms. It describes an autoregressive omni network and training/evaluations without total or active parameter counts. Broader audio/video/image-generation capabilities are not transferred to this text-output API snapshot.

sources.title: GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened the later original system-card PDF from the October 27, 2026 fresh cache; inspected GPT-4o comparison references and searched the complete text for parameter/count disclosures. The tables report performance rather than total or active parameters. The card discusses later ChatGPT GPT-4o versions, so those versions are not assumed identical to the August 2024 API snapshot.

sources.title: FILBENCH: Can LLMs Understand and Generate Filipino?
sources.publisher: Miranda et al.; EMNLP 2025 / Association for Computational Linguistics
sources.evidence: Original benchmark paper reopened October 27, 2026. Appendix A, Table 6 (PDF page 16) names the exact gpt-4o-2024-08-06 snapshot and leaves # Params (B) as a dash. The caption explicitly distinguishes total and active counts for MoE comparison models. This later research comparison supplies neither count for the exact snapshot; its blank cell is not a zero or a size inference.

sources.title: RAD-Bench: Evaluating Large Language Models’ Capabilities in Retrieval Augmented Dialogues
sources.publisher: Kuo et al.; MediaTek Research / NAACL 2025 Industry Track
sources.evidence: Original research paper reopened October 27, 2026. Table 2 (PDF page 5) explicitly labels Activated Params. and leaves GPT-4o blank. Section 4.1 says closed-model responses were collected in July 2024 and identifies a May 13 GPT-4o judge. The experiment therefore does not establish a count for the later August snapshot; retained only as a checked and rejected cross-model active-count lead.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity
sources.evidence: Original July 2026 revision reopened October 27, 2026. Abstract and Table 2 characterize the reported values as effective knowledge capacity in open-model-equivalent parameters, inferred from black-box factual recall and expressed as prediction bands. GPT-4o appears under a family label rather than the exact August snapshot. These calibrated capacity estimates are not published production total or active parameter specifications and are excluded.

name.note: Retain the catalog display name combining official product and immutable API snapshot date.

developer.note: Official launch and API documentation identify OpenAI.

family.note: The launch places the August snapshot in the GPT-4o series; replace generic gpt.

release_date.note: Exact snapshot release is explicitly described as today in the dated August 6 announcement; May 13 is the earlier family release.

open_weights.note: Hosted API release; OpenAI calls GPT-4o proprietary and identifies later gpt-oss as its first open-weight language models since GPT-2.

license.note: Descriptive service/model classification, not an SPDX identifier or downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: No published nominal total found for the exact snapshot in the fresh official release, API documentation, interpretability research or later comparisons. FILBENCH Table 6 explicitly leaves its count blank. SAE latents and black-box knowledge-capacity estimates do not measure production parameters; no named base lineage with a disclosed size was found.

active_parameters_b.note: No published nominal active count found for the exact snapshot. OpenAI’s 64 active SAE latents describe an auxiliary autoencoder. FILBENCH gives no count; RAD-Bench’s explicit active-count column is blank and its experiment predates this snapshot. Black-box capacity estimates and total-equals-active assumptions are excluded.

architecture.note: Broad Transformer classification follows OpenAI's documented inference mechanism explicitly applied to gpt-4o, whose current default is this snapshot. Operational evidence establishes a Transformer attention stack, not a complete inventory, exclusively Transformer layers or dense/MoE routing. The exact-snapshot SAE research supplies no routing disclosure.

context_window.note: Explicit context limit is 128,000 tokens; 16,384 is the separate maximum output length. Alias mapping binds the specification to the August snapshot.

modalities.note: Text/image inputs and text output describe this API snapshot. Add PDF under the existing catalog convention for supported API files; it is processed into extracted text and page images. Do not transfer broader omni-system audio/video or image-output capabilities.

reasoning.note: The official prompting guide explicitly identifies GPT-4o as a prior non-reasoning model. This denotes dedicated reasoning-token behavior, not inability to perform reasoning tasks or produce prompted visible steps.

tool_call.note: Both the original exact-snapshot launch and current bound alias documentation explicitly support function calling.

description.value: August 2024 GPT-4o API snapshot with text and image input, text output, function calling and Structured Outputs.
description.note: Plain factual description identifies snapshot and documented capabilities without promotional or unsupported size claims.

patch.notes: The gpt-4o alias defaults to this August 6, 2024 Structured Outputs snapshot. It supports 128,000-token context, text/image inputs and text output; PDF files are converted to text and page images. Broad Transformer structure is documented, but nominal total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed. SAE feature counts and black-box capacity estimates are not model parameters. OpenAI marks the snapshot deprecated with API removal scheduled for January 14, 2027.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retained explicit null total and active counts after fresh exact-snapshot official documentation, original interpretability and system-card checks, and bounded later research searches. FILBENCH leaves the exact snapshot’s size blank; RAD-Bench predates it, and IKP reports inferred knowledge capacity rather than production size. Preserved all 12 other audited fields.
